kurzbeschreibung: The Ötztal is Tirol’s longest side valley—a realm of superlatives featuring mighty glaciers, the 3,768 m high Wildspitze, World Cup hub Sölden, and alpine wellness at Aqua Dome.
beschreibung: The Ötztal stretches for 65 kilometers as the longest side valley of the Inn Valley and ranks among the most spectacular high-alpine destinations in Europe. Framed by 250 three-thousand-meter peaks, the mountains culminate in the Wildspitze (3,768 m), the highest summit in North Tirol. From the sunny valley entrance at Oetz with the picturesque Piburger See, the valley continues past Umhausen with the Stuibenfall—Tirol’s tallest waterfall—and the wide basin of Längenfeld up to the internationally renowned winter sports resorts of Sölden and Gurgl. Winter highlights include the twin glacier ski areas of Rettenbach and Tiefenbach and the BIG 3 observation platforms above 3,000 meters. Culturally, the archaeological Ötzi Village in Umhausen brings the era of the famed iceman to life.
tipps: The Stuibenfall near Umhausen is Tirol’s highest waterfall with a 159 m drop—explored via a suspension bridge and 700 steps.
The Aqua Dome in Längenfeld offers futuristic thermal spa architecture with floating outdoor basin bowls and healing waters.
The James Bond cinematic installation 007 ELEMENTS atop Gaislachkogl (3,048 m) in Sölden delves inside the original Spectre filming location.
empfehlungen: A must-do: Drive up the Ötztal Glacier Road to the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers or ascend Gaislachkogl to experience 007 ELEMENTS. For pure relaxation, unwind at the Aqua Dome thermal spa in Längenfeld admiring panoramic alpine vistas.
umgebung: The Ötztal branches southward from the Inntal at Haiming and extends to the main alpine ridge bordering South Tyrol (Italy). Neighboring regions: Imst (north), Pitztal (west), Stubaital (east), and South Tyrol via the scenic Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road (2,474 m).
